title: The Toad's Marks
prompt: Each evening the old toad counts the fireflies as they wake, scratching a single mark into a flat stone for every new one, but he records only the first letter of each number's name.
Tonight the stone already reads, in order: O, T, T, F, F, S, S, E.
What letter does the toad scratch next?
hints: These are not random scratches. Try reading them aloud, in order, and listen for something familiar.
Remember what the toad is doing the whole time: counting upward, one firefly at a time.
O is for one, T for two, T for three, F for four, F for five, S for six, S for seven, E for eight. What letter begins the next number?
solution_lede:
The marks look like a code, and they are, but a gentle one. The toad is simply counting, and writing down the first letter of each number's name as he goes.

Read in order, O, T, T, F, F, S, S, E are the initials of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. The very next number is nine, so the next mark is the letter N.

solution_steps.body: Match each letter to a counting number by its name: O is one, T is two, T is three, F is four, F is five, S is six, S is seven, E is eight.
The sequence is just the counting numbers in order, recorded by their first letter.
The number after eight is nine, whose name begins with N. The toad scratches N.
